column8: Named bundle of options (see --list-presets): applied above the saved config file and below environment and command line. Empty = none.
Proportions of the vessel. slab: broad and flat. tiered: a tall superstructure over a deep drop. long: lean and very long. auto: drawn per chapter.
The one structure each vessel is remembered by: a ring the runway passes under, or three tall fins on the superstructure. auto: drawn per chapter.
Colour family of the windows and lights. harmonic: a colourway generated per chapter (windows at one hue and near its complement; the gate follows it). auto: drawn per chapter among all of them.
Which side of the frame the vessel appears on, and so which side the runway and aperture are on. auto: drawn per chapter.
The world below the vessel, or none (stars only). auto: drawn per chapter.
Light inside the hall: hangar (cool daylight shafts) or foundry (amber shafts). auto: drawn per chapter.
Length of one chapter in arc seconds, 380 to 900; the extra time goes to the quiet room. 0 = automatic (390 to 420, from the seed).
Wall seconds per arc second: 2 plays the whole arc (and every motion in it) at half speed, 0.7 at about 1.4 times the speed. The lower limit keeps every blinking light at or below 1 Hz.
Starting hue of the gate's colour path, 0 to 359; it still drifts slowly (<= 0.03 Hz). -1 = automatic.
Contrast and saturation of the gate, 0.3 to 1. The gate never exceeds a display value of 0.85 or a mean near 0.45 at any setting.
Multiplier on the number of visible stars.
auto: every chapter re-seeds at the end of the quiet room (new vessel, palette, planet, side). fixed: every chapter repeats the first one.
Detail tier. auto follows the GPU class of this machine (NCZ_SHADER_QUALITY still overrides it).
Testing and captures: begin the run this many arc seconds into the first chapter (for example 45 for the hull pass, 200 for the hall, 300 for the gate). 0 = from the start.

Fixes the run's randomness so a run can be repeated exactly (with the same preset and options). 0 = a new seed (1 to 999999) every run; the seed in use is logged to standard error, so any run can be replayed with --seed.
